newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer, rate hike 'factored in'.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer, rate hike 'factored in'.

text.p: COMEX copper settled firmer in fairly light volume, the market underpinned by a continued fall in LME stocks, traders said.
On Tuesday LME stocks fell 4,300 tonnes to 183,475 tonnes, in line with trader expectations.
COMEX copper stopped trading a few minutes before the Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee decided to hike the interest rate by 0.25 percent.
"The interest rate scenario is pretty much in the market," Bette Raptopoulos of Prudential Securities said.
The market may see some light profit-taking early Wednesday, but would then continue with its choppy, upwardly biased course, Raptopoulos added.

Although copper is a key industrial metal and vulnerable to higher interest rates, low inventory and continued good demand, especially in the United States, would underpin the market for now, traders said.
COMEX May copper settled 1.95 cents firmer at 112.90 cents a pound, traded 113.20 to 110.75 cents. Spot March went out 2.10 cents higher at 119.50 cents.
Volume was estimated at 8,500 lots compared to Monday's 5,376 lots.
Traders said activity was choppy due to the light volume on COMEX and LME, and this was likely to continue until after the Easter Holiday.
COMEX and LME are shut Friday, with LME also shut next Monday.
